claim: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines the Speech Transmission Index model, test signals, measurement and prediction methods for objective rating of speech intelligibility in sound system equipment.
source_title: IEC 60268-16:2020 Sound system equipment — Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines the STI model, test signals, measurement and prediction methods for objective rating of speech intelligibility.
caveat: Full standard is paywalled; scope statement is public on IEC webstore.

claim: IEC 60268-16 categorizes STI values in five qualitative bands: Bad (<0.30), Poor (0.30–0.45), Fair (0.45–0.60), Good (0.60–0.75), and Excellent (>0.75).
source_title: IEC 60268-16: Measuring Speech Intelligibility (STI/STIPA)
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268-16 defines five qualitative categories: Bad (STI below 0.30), Poor (0.30 to 0.45), Fair (0.45 to 0.60), Good (0.60 to 0.75), and Excellent (above 0.75).
caveat: Secondary summary of a paywalled standard; verify against IEC 60268-16:2020 primary text before publication.

claim: STIPA (Speech Transmission Index for Public Address) allows a single-point measurement in approximately 10–20 seconds using a specially designed test signal with two modulation frequencies per octave band.
source_title: IEC 60268-16: Measuring Speech Intelligibility (STI/STIPA)
supporting_excerpt: STIPA (STI for Public Address) [is] a faster alternative using a specially designed test signal with two modulation frequencies per octave band (14 total). Using this signal, a single measurement is made, with total measurement time taking ~10-20 seconds.
caveat: Secondary reference; primary source is IEC 60268-16:2020.

claim: NFPA 72 requires a minimum voice intelligibility rating consistent with STI 0.45 (Fair on the Common Intelligibility Scale) at all occupant locations for emergency voice systems, with a design target of 0.70 STI over 90 percent of the covered area.
source_title: Mass Notification: Intelligibility is NOT Optional
supporting_excerpt: NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code requires a 0.70 Speech Transmission Index [STI] minimum so that a message is intelligible and therefore understood... The target is 0.70 STI in 90% of the area, with an absolute floor of 0.50 STI... [other guidance:] NFPA 72 requires a minimum intelligibility rating consistent with STI of 0.45 or higher (Fair on the CIS scale) at all occupant locations.
data_vintage: cites NFPA 72 editions post-2010; verify against current MWAA-adopted edition
denominator: at all occupant locations / 90% of covered area
caveat: Trade publication cites multiple thresholds; MWAA should verify against the specific NFPA 72 edition adopted in the jurisdictional code cycle.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends maintaining a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges.
source_title: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems — Chapter 3, Speech Intelligibility
supporting_excerpt: The study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges to ensure that announcements are clearly audible to passengers.
caveat: Chapter 3 threshold applies to a specific terminal typology; other typologies have different recommended thresholds within the same report.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport policy was launched in 2018 and implemented through 2019–2020, and includes localizing paging so passengers at A gates do not hear announcements from B gates (except final calls), and tenant rules limiting retail 'sound footprint' and background music.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise — Travelers Say It Changed Everything
supporting_excerpt: In 2018, SFO launched its Quiet Airport policy which it implemented throughout 2019 and 2020... The SFO Customer Care team realigned where public announcements would be made to page passengers only in necessary areas of the airport. For example if you're at an A gate, you're not going to be hearing announcements from the B gates with the exception of final calls... The airport developed new rules for businesses inside the airport that would limit their 'sound footprint' and their use of music.
caveat: Trade coverage; primary SFO policy document should be sourced for the final article.

claim: SFO reports its Quiet Airport policy produced approximately a 40 percent reduction in announcements at gate seating areas and eliminated over 90 minutes of announcements per day in the International Terminal.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise — Travelers Say It Changed Everything
supporting_excerpt: This resulted in a 40% reduction of announcements at gate seating areas and 90 minutes of reduction in the whole terminal each day. More specifically, they've eliminated over 90 minutes of unnecessary announcements a day in the International Terminal.
data_vintage: reflects SFO reporting for the 2019–2020 implementation window
denominator: gate seating area announcements; International Terminal daily announcement time
caveat: Reported figure; measurement methodology was not verified in primary sources for this brief.

claim: Some SFO passengers report the Quiet Airport policy causes them to miss information such as gate changes.

caveat: Secondary reporting; anecdotal passenger complaints, not a measured missed-boarding rate.

data_vintage: reflects 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design
airport_or_entity: US Access Board / ADA (applies to airport assembly areas)
